UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                      )
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C                            )                 Docket No. ER26-3515-000
                                                      )



                       MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND ANSWER
                             OF ADVANCED ENERGY UNITED

         Pursuant to Rule 212 and 213 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedures,1 Advanced Energy United2 (“United”)

submits this motion for leave to answer and limited answer to the answer of PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) in the above-captioned proceeding.3 United submits this limited

answer because PJM’s Answer mischaracterizes the relief United actually requested regarding

customer-sponsored Peak Shaving Adjustments (“PSA”),4 and because PJM’s stated rationale for

declining that relief is inconsistent with positions PJM takes elsewhere in the same Answer.

I.       MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER

         Although Rule 213(a)(2) does not generally permit an answer to an answer, the

Commission grants leave where good cause is shown, including where an answer assists the

Commission’s decision-making process by correcting the record or supplying information the

  18 C.F.R. § 385.211
2
  Advanced Energy United is a national association of businesses that are making the energy we use secure, clean,
and affordable. Advanced Energy United is the only industry association in the United States that represents the full
range of advanced energy technologies and services, both grid-scale and distributed. Advanced energy includes
energy efficiency, demand response, energy storage, wind, solar, hydro, nuclear, electric vehicles, and more. The
views expressed in these comments reflect the position of Advanced Energy United, but do not necessarily reflect
the views of any particular member with respect to any issue.
3
  Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER26-3515-000, (Sept. 23,
2026) (“PJM Answer”)
4
  Comments of Advanced Energy United, Docket No. ER26-3515-000, at 3 (September 3, 2026). (“United
Comments”)
                                                                                                                    1
 Commission needs to resolve a disputed issue.5 Good cause exists here. PJM’s Answer directly

addresses and rejects a specific request in United’s comments6, but does so by responding to a

different, broader proposal than the one United actually made, and by relying on a rationale PJM

does not apply consistently elsewhere in that same Answer. Leaving that mischaracterization and

inconsistency unaddressed risks leading the Commission to resolve this issue based on an

inaccurate description of the relief United requested. United accordingly requests leave to file

this limited answer.

II.     ANSWER

        United's answer addresses three distinct flaws in how PJM’s Answer treats Peak Shaving

Adjustments (“PSA”) under IRAS, each independent of the others. First, PJM’s rejection of

PSAs as a verifiable tool to reduce resource adequacy need rests on a distinction PJM does not

apply consistently elsewhere in its own Answer. Second, PJM defends against a broader proposal

to treat PSA as a substitute for large loads supporting new capacity through Bring Your Own

New Capacity (“BYONC”), rather than the narrower one United actually requested, which was

that PSAs be taken into account when calculating IRAS exposure. Third, PJM treats PSA and

BYONC as equivalent rather than recognizing that they address the same capacity gap from

different sides and thus crediting one does not require relaxing requirements for the other. Taken




5
  See, e.g., PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 189 FERC ¶ 61,110, at P 22 (2024) (accepting answers to protests and
answers because they assisted the Commission in its decision-making process).
6
  PJM Answer at 47-48 (citing United Comments at 3).
                                                                                                                 2
 together, these flaws show that PJM’s Answer does not actually respond to the issue United

raised.

             A. PJM’s Rejection of PSA Credit to Displace IRAS Need Rests on an Internal
                Inconsistency in PJM’s Own Answer

          PJM’s Answer rejects crediting PSA against a New Large Load’s IRAS exposure on the

ground that PSA amounts are “adjustments to PJM’s load forecasts, not resources that may

participate in RPM Auctions,” and are not a “real-time dispatchable product.”7 PJM reasons that

this distinction settles the question: because PSA does not clear an auction and cannot be called

upon in real time, it categorically cannot reduce the capacity need giving rise to IRAS

curtailment.

          PJM’s own Answer, however, shows that this distinction does not actually settle

anything. In the same filing, PJM confirms that it already permits qualifying PSA MW “that

qualify for an opt-out to potentially reduce the identified 2027/2028 Delivery Year capacity

shortfall for which the RBP will procure.”8 That is, PJM already treats a PSA value, the identical

kind of forecast adjustment PJM now calls too unreliable to be taken into account under IRAS,

as sound enough to shrink the actual, binding quantity of capacity PJM goes out and procures

through the companion Reliability Backstop Procurement mechanism.9 Just as a PSA value

serves to reduce how much capacity PJM is targeting to procure under the RBP, it should be

factored into how much of a load’s demand counts as unmet capacity need under IRAS.

          PJM offers no explanation for why the same PSA value should be treated as germane in

one proceeding and irrelevant in the other. Both the RBP procurement target and the IRAS



7
  Id.
8
  Id.
9
  See, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address Resource Adequacy Concerns
Stemming from Large Loads, Docket No. ER26-3380-000, (July 31, 2026) (“PJM RBP”)
                                                                                                             3
 Eligible New Large Load Amount are wholesale-level calculations of how much capacity is

actually needed to serve PJM’s system given the unmet demand from New Large Loads. PJM

designed RBP and IRAS as companion mechanisms addressing the same shortfall, and PJM

cannot now maintain two incompatible positions on the reliability of the same underlying data

depending on which mechanism is more convenient in each instance.

           If a qualifying PSA value is sound enough to reduce PJM’s own procurement target

under RBP, it is sound enough to reduce the capacity need attributable to the New Large Load

that sponsored it. The same treatment of PSA that already applies under RBP is equally relevant

here and should be incorporated as a means to reduce IRAS exposure.

               B. PJM’s “Not Dispatchable” Rationale Answers a Request United Did Not
                  Make

           PJM’s Answer builds its rejection of PSA credit around PSA’s unsuitability as a

substitute for BYONC, a tradable, must-offer capacity resource that PJM’s Tariff requires to

satisfy specific capacity market obligations.10 On that framing, PSA fails because it cannot be

dispatched, cannot clear an auction, and carries none of the ongoing capacity-market obligations

BYONC carries.

           PJM is drawing an unnecessary parallel between BYONC and PSA, and responding to a

request United never made. United’s comments did not ask PJM to treat PSA as BYONC, to

permit PSA to participate in RPM Auctions, or to make PSA dispatchable during an IRAS

Action. United asked only that PJM’s Tariff “specify that the deduction under this formula for a

qualifying Peak Shaving Adjustment or comparable state-authorized reduction shall equal the

MW value calculated and verified by PJM pursuant to its applicable procedures.”11 That is a



10
     PJM Answer at 47-48
11
     United Comments at 4.
                                                                                                   4
 request to reflect an already-measured reduction in resource-adequacy need, not a request to

convert PSA into a capacity product it was never designed to be.

        The distinction matters because PJM’s own Eligible New Large Load Amount

calculation is not itself a real-time dispatch decision. It is a forecast-based determination, built

from registration data, load forecasts, and capacity commitments, that fixes a load’s exposure

before any Interim Resource Adequacy Alert is ever called.12 A qualifying PSA reduces the

underlying capacity need that calculation is meant to measure before any such Alert occurs, in

exactly the same way BYONC and Allocated RBP UCAP MW do. Whether PSA could be

dispatched during an emergency is beside the point; the reduction it represents has already

occurred by the time PJM performs the calculation PJM proposes to use.

        United respectfully requests that the Commission consider the argument in our original

filing, which was that the IRAS exposure calculation should take into account a verified

reduction in resource-adequacy need resulting from PSA, rather than PJM’s mischaracterization

of that request as an ask to treat PSA as a dispatchable capacity resource.

            C. PSA and BYONC Are Complementary, Not Competing, Categories

        PJM’s Answer proceeds as though recognizing PSA within the Eligible New Large Load

Amount formula would require treating PSA as a substitute for BYONC, competing for the same

role BYONC already fills. It would not. BYONC and PSA address the same underlying problem,

i.e., the gap between a New Large Load’s demand and the capacity available to serve it, from

two different directions, and nothing in United’s request asks PJM to blur that distinction.




12
  Proposed RAA, Attachment DD-4, § V(b) (PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER26-3515-000, (Aug. 13,
2026)")
                                                                                                            5
          BYONC works on the supply side: it adds new capacity to the system to match or offset a

load’s demand. PSA works on the demand side: it reduces the capacity PJM must otherwise

procure, or the amount of curtailment that may be necessary. A load that brings 50 MW of

BYONC and a load that supports the reduction of the zonal or EDC peak by 50 MW through a

qualifying PSA arrive at an identical outcome, from PJM’s perspective: the load’s otherwise-

unmet capacity need shrinks by the same amount. The mechanism differs, but the resource-

adequacy benefit does not, and thus large loads should be given the same credit. PJM itself

recognized PSA and BYONC as different sides of the same coin in its Transmittal Letter when it

excluded any locations from “new” BYONC status that had previously helped “reduce the

amount of capacity needed to meet the PJM Region Reliability Requirement through a Peak

Shaving Adjustment or Price Responsive Demand.”13

         Recognizing the verified benefit of PSA does not require PJM to loosen any of the

requirements applicable to BYONC, which would remain the only pathway to recognize a New

Large Load’s contribution to bringing actual new capacity to the system, subject to must-offer

requirements, capacity market participation, and the ten-year commitment discussed above.14

PSA would remain what it already is under PJM’s own rules, a verified reduction to the forecast

peak demand from which a load’s capacity need is calculated.15 Because PJM already relies on

PSA as a demand-side decrement in the RPM today, alongside other demand-side measures such

as Price Responsive Demand (“PRD”),16 it is not a speculative or unverified figure. Rather, it is


13
   Transmittal Letter at 54 (citing Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD-4, §§ VI(b)(ii)(1)-(2))
14
   Id at 43-44.
15
   Id at 47-48; see also, PJM Manual 19, Load Forecasting and Analysis, § 3.2 (explaining, “In cases where a zone
contains a peak shaving program with an approved Peak Shaving Adjustment Plan, the zone’s forecast will be
adjusted to reflect the program’s impact.”).
16
   PJM committed 106.5 MW UCAP of PRD in the 2027/2028 Base Residual Auction (“BRA”) PJM
Interconnection, L.L.C., 2027/2028 Base Residual Auction Report, at 3 n.1 (Dec. 17, 2025). PJM describes PRD as
“a predictable change in the amount of electricity used, not as additional generation.” PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.,
“Price Responsive Demand Fact Sheet” at 2 (March 23, 2017).
                                                                                                                       6
 tied to a specific, state-authorized program, triggered by an objective measure, the actual

maximum daily temperature-humidity index for the relevant zone, scored over a rolling three-

year period, and verified through PJM’s own applicable procedures.17 PSA does not need to be

dispatchable or tradable to be a reliable input into a forecast-based formula that is not itself a

real-time dispatch determination. It only needs to be measured accurately, and PJM’s own rules

already ensure that it is.

        Consideration of both BYONC and PSA as complementary tools will result in a more

accurate measure of a load’s true, net capacity need than a Tariff that recognizes only one side of

that calculation. The success and impact of PJM’s IRAS proposal depends on getting that net

figure right. The purpose of the Eligible New Large Load Amount formula is to identify how

much of a load’s demand remains genuinely uncovered.18 A formula that credits new supply but

ignores a verified reduction in peak demand does not measure that figure accurately, it

systematically overstates it for any load that has taken real, verified steps to reduce the regional

shortfall. PJM should be directed to correct the formula so that it reflects both halves of a New

Large Load’s actual net capacity need. Failure to do so will result in a harmful over-estimation of

IRAS need while diminishing the incentive for New Large Loads to pursue PSA as a mechanism

to affordably and quickly reduce pressure on the strained PJM grid.

III.    CONCLUSION

        PJM’s Answer does not resolve the issue United raised; it responds to a different request

while relying on a rationale PJM does not apply consistently elsewhere in the same filing. United

asks the Commission to direct PJM to credit qualifying, verified PSA values in the Eligible New

18
  Proposed RAA, Attachment DD-4, § V(b) (PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER26-3515-000, Aug. 13,
2026).

 Large Load Amount formula on the same basis PJM already applies under RBP. United

respectfully requests that the Commission grant this motion for leave to answer and accept this

answer.



       Respectfully submitted,
